newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India GDRs drift as local shares rise.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India GDRs drift as local shares rise.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts paused for breath on Tuesday, trading sideways, with little investor interest despite another strong run in local markets, dealers said.
"There was some buying of blue chips but generally investors hung back," said one dealer.
This came despite another rally in Bombay, which followed a Monday rise of three percent with a one percent gain Tuesday.
But dealers see the GDR market as likely to catch up Bombay shares.
"I certainly don't see the premium narrowing from here," one dealer said.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 0.07 points lower at 89.98, down 0.08 percent, with the premium over the local market at 24.89 percent from 25.31 percent.
Bombay's benchmark index rose 44.77 points to 4,300.86.
Hindalco gained 68 cents to $35.70/$36.70 and Telco rose 12 cents to $15.00/$15.75.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index closed 2.43 points higher, or 3.26 percent, at 76.91 points, a premium of 39.58 percent over the local market.
Korean shares were helped by the release of trade figures which showed the first monthly surplus since December 1994.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index finished 1.54 points lower at 130.66, representing a discount to the local market of 1.16 percent.
Taiwan's stock market was closed Tuesday for a holiday.
